subject: food-technology
topicDisplay: Food Safety Food Science And Special Diets
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Bacteria in the danger zone can roughly double in number every:
questions.explain: In ideal conditions bacteria can divide approximately every 10-20 minutes, so numbers rise rapidly.

questions.q: By UK law, which of the following must always be clearly emphasised on food labels?
questions.explain: Food labels must clearly highlight any of the 14 major allergens (such as nuts, milk, eggs) present.

questions.q: The thickening of a sauce when starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating is called:
questions.explain: Gelatinisation is when starch granules absorb liquid, swell and burst on heating to thicken a sauce.

questions.q: Which of these is the best example of good personal hygiene in the kitchen?
options: Washing hands before handling food and after touching raw meat
Wearing the same apron for weeks
Tasting food with the same spoon repeatedly
questions.explain: Washing hands thoroughly before cooking and after handling raw meat helps prevent the spread of bacteria.

questions.q: Food prepared according to Jewish dietary law is described as:
questions.explain: Kosher food follows Jewish dietary laws, which forbid pork and the mixing of meat and dairy.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of cross-contamination?
options: Using the same chopping board for raw chicken and salad without washing it
questions.explain: Cross-contamination is the transfer of bacteria from raw food to ready-to-eat food, such as via an unwashed board.

questions.q: A cut apple turns brown when left in air. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Enzymic browning happens when enzymes in cut fruit react with oxygen in the air, turning the surface brown.

questions.q: A 'use-by' date on a food product tells you:
options: The last date the food is safe to eat
When the food should be frozen
The date by which the food is at its best quality only
questions.explain: A use-by date is a safety date; eating the food after it is unsafe even if it looks fine.

questions.q: Which type of food is classed as 'high-risk' for food poisoning?
questions.explain: High-risk foods are moist, protein-rich, ready-to-eat foods such as cooked meat and cooked rice.

questions.q: A correctly working refrigerator should keep food at approximately:
questions.explain: A fridge should run at about 0-5C to slow the growth of bacteria.

questions.q: Lactose intolerance is the inability to properly digest the sugar found in:
questions.explain: Lactose is the natural sugar in milk and dairy, which people with lactose intolerance cannot digest well.

questions.q: Grilling and toasting cook food mainly by which method of heat transfer?
questions.explain: Grilling cooks food by radiation, where heat waves travel directly from the heat source to the food.
